newsitem.title: UK: Cook says single market high priority for Britain.
newsitem.headline: Cook says single market high priority for Britain.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said removing obstacles to completion of the European Union single market, especially in telecommunications, financial services and energy, would be a high priority for Britain's presidency of the EU next year.
Addressing a Trades Union Congress (TUC) conference on "Social Europe," he said the EU was Britain's most important export market.

"It is therefore very important for working people in Britain that we remove those obstacles that are still there in the way of..maximising..exports to the Continent, particularly tackling the regulations in telecommunications, financial services and energy which prevent Britain competing on a level playing field," Cook said.
These were sectors in which the UK was strong and completion of the single market would be in the interest of employment in Britain.
Britain will take on the presidency of the EU for six months from January 1, 1998.
Cook said the other priority of the presidency would be enlargement of the EU to include former communist countries in central and eastern Europe.
